personae.name: KING
personae.blurb: of Navarre, also known as Ferdinand BEROWNE, Lord attending on the King

personae.name: Lords
personae.blurb: Blackamoors, Officers and Others, Attendants on the King and Princess

lines.text: Enter Ferdinand, King of Navarre, Berowne, Longaville and Dumaine.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Let fame, that all hunt after in their lives,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Live registered upon our brazen tombs,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: And then grace us in the disgrace of death;

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: When, spite of cormorant devouring time,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Th’ endeavour of this present breath may buy

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: That honour which shall bate his scythe’s keen edge,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: And make us heirs of all eternity.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Therefore, brave conquerors, for so you are

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: That war against your own affections

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: And the huge army of the world’s desires,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Our late edict shall strongly stand in force.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Navarre shall be the wonder of the world;

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Our court shall be a little academe,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Still and contemplative in living art.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: You three, Berowne, Dumaine and Longaville,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Have sworn for three years’ term to live with me,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: My fellow-scholars, and to keep those statutes

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: That are recorded in this schedule here.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Your oaths are passed, and now subscribe your names,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: That his own hand may strike his honour down

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: That violates the smallest branch herein.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: If you are armed to do as sworn to do,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Subscribe to your deep oaths, and keep it too.

lines.speaker: LONGAVILLE
lines.text: I am resolved. ’Tis but a three years’ fast.

lines.speaker: LONGAVILLE
lines.text: The mind shall banquet, though the body pine.

lines.speaker: LONGAVILLE
lines.text: Fat paunches have lean pates, and dainty bits

lines.speaker: LONGAVILLE
lines.text: Make rich the ribs, but bankrupt quite the wits.
[_He signs._]

lines.speaker: DUMAINE
lines.text: My loving lord, Dumaine is mortified.

lines.speaker: DUMAINE
lines.text: The grosser manner of these world’s delights

lines.speaker: DUMAINE
lines.text: He throws upon the gross world’s baser slaves.

lines.speaker: DUMAINE
lines.text: To love, to wealth, to pomp, I pine and die,

lines.speaker: DUMAINE
lines.text: With all these living in philosophy.
[_He signs._]

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: I can but say their protestation over.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: So much, dear liege, I have already sworn,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: That is, to live and study here three years.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: But there are other strict observances:

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: As not to see a woman in that term,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Which I hope well is not enrolled there;

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: And one day in a week to touch no food,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: And but one meal on every day beside,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: The which I hope is not enrolled there;

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: And then to sleep but three hours in the night,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: And not be seen to wink of all the day,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: When I was wont to think no harm all night,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: And make a dark night too of half the day,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Which I hope well is not enrolled there.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: O, these are barren tasks, too hard to keep,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Not to see ladies, study, fast, not sleep.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Your oath is passed to pass away from these.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Let me say no, my liege, an if you please.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: I only swore to study with your Grace

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: And stay here in your court for three years’ space.

lines.speaker: LONGAVILLE
lines.text: You swore to that, Berowne, and to the rest.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: By yea and nay, sir, then I swore in jest.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: What is the end of study, let me know?

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Why, that to know which else we should not know.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Things hid and barred, you mean, from common sense?

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Ay, that is study’s god-like recompense.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Come on, then, I will swear to study so,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: To know the thing I am forbid to know:

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: As thus, to study where I well may dine,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: When I to feast expressly am forbid;

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Or study where to meet some mistress fine,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: When mistresses from common sense are hid;

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Or, having sworn too hard-a-keeping oath,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Study to break it, and not break my troth.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: If study’s gain be thus, and this be so,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Study knows that which yet it doth not know.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Swear me to this, and I will ne’er say no.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: These be the stops that hinder study quite,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: And train our intellects to vain delight.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Why, all delights are vain, but that most vain

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Which, with pain purchased, doth inherit pain:

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: As painfully to pore upon a book

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: To seek the light of truth, while truth the while

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Doth falsely blind the eyesight of his look.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Light seeking light doth light of light beguile;

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: So, ere you find where light in darkness lies,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Your light grows dark by losing of your eyes.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Study me how to please the eye indeed

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: By fixing it upon a fairer eye,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Who dazzling so, that eye shall be his heed,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: And give him light that it was blinded by.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Study is like the heaven’s glorious sun,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: That will not be deep-searched with saucy looks;

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Small have continual plodders ever won,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Save base authority from others’ books.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: These earthly godfathers of heaven’s lights,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: That give a name to every fixed star,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Have no more profit of their shining nights

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Than those that walk and wot not what they are.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Too much to know is to know naught but fame,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: And every godfather can give a name.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: How well he’s read, to reason against reading.

lines.speaker: DUMAINE
lines.text: Proceeded well, to stop all good proceeding.

lines.speaker: LONGAVILLE
lines.text: He weeds the corn, and still lets grow the weeding.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: The spring is near when green geese are a-breeding.

lines.speaker: DUMAINE
lines.text: How follows that?

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Fit in his place and time.

lines.speaker: DUMAINE
lines.text: In reason nothing.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Something then in rhyme.

lines.speaker: LONGAVILLE
lines.text: Berowne is like an envious sneaping frost

lines.speaker: LONGAVILLE
lines.text: That bites the first-born infants of the spring.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Well, say I am. Why should proud summer boast

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Before the birds have any cause to sing?

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Why should I joy in any abortive birth?

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: At Christmas I no more desire a rose

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Than wish a snow in May’s new-fangled shows,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: But like of each thing that in season grows.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: So you, to study now it is too late,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Climb o’er the house to unlock the little gate.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Well, sit you out. Go home, Berowne. Adieu.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: No, my good lord, I have sworn to stay with you,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: And though I have for barbarism spoke more

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Than for that angel knowledge you can say,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Yet confident I’ll keep what I have sworn

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: And bide the penance of each three years’ day.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Give me the paper, let me read the same,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: And to the strictest decrees I’ll write my name.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: How well this yielding rescues thee from shame.
[_Reads_.]

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: _Item, That no woman shall come within a mile of my court._

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Hath this been proclaimed?

lines.speaker: LONGAVILLE
lines.text: Four days ago.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Let’s see the penalty. [_Reads_.] _On pain of losing her tongue._ Who

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: devised this penalty?

lines.speaker: LONGAVILLE
lines.text: Marry, that did I.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Sweet lord, and why?

lines.speaker: LONGAVILLE
lines.text: To fright them hence with that dread penalty.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: A dangerous law against gentility.
[_Reads_.]

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: _Item, If any man be seen to talk with a woman within the

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: term of three years, he shall endure such public shame as the rest of

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: the court can possibly devise._

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: This article, my liege, yourself must break,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: For well you know here comes in embassy

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: The French King’s daughter, with yourself to speak—

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: A mild of grace and complete majesty—

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: About surrender up of Aquitaine

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: To her decrepit, sick, and bedrid father.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Therefore this article is made in vain,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Or vainly comes th’ admired Princess hither.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: What say you, lords? Why, this was quite forgot.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: So study evermore is overshot.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: While it doth study to have what it would,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: It doth forget to do the thing it should;

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: And when it hath the thing it hunteth most,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: ’Tis won as towns with fire: so won, so lost.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: We must of force dispense with this decree.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: She must lie here on mere necessity.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Necessity will make us all forsworn

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Three thousand times within this three years’ space;

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: For every man with his affects is born,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Not by might mastered, but by special grace.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: If I break faith, this word shall speak for me:

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: I am forsworn on mere necessity.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: So to the laws at large I write my name,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: And he that breaks them in the least degree

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Stands in attainder of eternal shame.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Suggestions are to other as to me;

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: But I believe, although I seem so loath,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: I am the last that will last keep his oath.
[_He signs._]

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: But is there no quick recreation granted?

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Ay, that there is. Our court, you know, is haunted

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: With a refined traveller of Spain,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: A man in all the world’s new fashion planted,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: That hath a mint of phrases in his brain;

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: One who the music of his own vain tongue

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Doth ravish like enchanting harmony,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: A man of complements, whom right and wrong

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Have chose as umpire of their mutiny.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: This child of fancy, that Armado hight,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: For interim to our studies shall relate

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: In high-born words the worth of many a knight

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: From tawny Spain lost in the world’s debate.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: How you delight, my lords, I know not, I,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: But I protest I love to hear him lie,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: And I will use him for my minstrelsy.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Armado is a most illustrious wight,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: A man of fire-new words, fashion’s own knight.

lines.speaker: LONGAVILLE
lines.text: Costard the swain and he shall be our sport,

lines.speaker: LONGAVILLE
lines.text: And so to study three years is but short.
Enter Dull, a Constable, with a letter, and Costard.

lines.speaker: DULL
lines.text: Which is the Duke’s own person?

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: This, fellow. What wouldst?

lines.speaker: DULL
lines.text: I myself reprehend his own person, for I am his Grace’s farborough. But

lines.speaker: DULL
lines.text: I would see his own person in flesh and blood.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: This is he.

lines.speaker: DULL
lines.text: Signior Arm… Arm… commends you. There’s villainy abroad. This letter

lines.speaker: DULL
lines.text: will tell you more.

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: Sir, the contempts thereof are as touching me.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: A letter from the magnificent Armado.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: How long soever the matter, I hope in God for high words.

lines.speaker: LONGAVILLE
lines.text: A high hope for a low heaven. God grant us patience!

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: To hear, or forbear laughing?

lines.speaker: LONGAVILLE
lines.text: To hear meekly, sir, and to laugh moderately, or to forbear both.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Well, sir, be it as the style shall give us cause to climb in the

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: merriness.

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: The matter is to me, sir, as concerning Jaquenetta. The manner of it

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: is, I was taken with the manner.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: In what manner?

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: In manner and form following, sir, all those three. I was seen with her

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: in the manor-house, sitting with her upon the form, and taken following

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: her into the park, which, put together, is “in manner and form

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: following”. Now, sir, for the manner. It is the manner of a man to

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: speak to a woman. For the form—in some form.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: For the “following”, sir?

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: As it shall follow in my correction, and God defend the right!

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Will you hear this letter with attention?

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: As we would hear an oracle.

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: Such is the simplicity of man to hearken after the flesh.
[_Reads_.]

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: _Great deputy, the welkin’s vicegerent and sole dominator of

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Navarre, my soul’s earth’s god and body’s fostering patron—_

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: Not a word of Costard yet.
[_Reads_.]

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: _So it is—_

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: It may be so; but if he say it is so, he is, in telling true, but so.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Peace!

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: Be to me, and every man that dares not fight.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: No words!

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: Of other men’s secrets, I beseech you.
[_Reads_.]

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: _So it is, besieged with sable-coloured melancholy, I did

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: commend the black-oppressing humour to the most wholesome physic of thy

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: health-giving air; and, as I am a gentleman, betook myself to walk. The

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: time when? About the sixth hour, when beasts most graze, birds best

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: peck, and men sit down to that nourishment which is called supper. So

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: much for the time when. Now for the ground which? Which, I mean, I

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: walked upon. It is ycleped thy park. Then for the place, where? Where,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: I mean, I did encounter that obscene and most preposterous event that

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: draweth from my snow-white pen the ebon-coloured ink, which here thou

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: viewest, beholdest, surveyest, or seest. But to the place where? It

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: standeth north-north-east and by east from the west corner of thy

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: curious-knotted garden. There did I see that low-spirited swain, that

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: base minnow of thy mirth—_

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: Me?
[_Reads_.]

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: _That unlettered small-knowing soul—_

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: Me?
[_Reads_.]

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: _That shallow vassal—_

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: Still me?
[_Reads_.]

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: _Which, as I remember, hight Costard—_

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: O me!
[_Reads_.]

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: _Sorted and consorted, contrary to thy established

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: proclaimed edict and continent canon, which with, O, with—but with this

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: I passion to say wherewith—_

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: With a wench.
[_Reads_.]

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: _With a child of our grandmother Eve, a female; or, for thy

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: more sweet understanding, a woman. Him, I, as my ever-esteemed duty

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: pricks me on, have sent to thee, to receive the meed of punishment, by

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: thy sweet Grace’s officer, Antony Dull, a man of good repute, carriage,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: bearing, and estimation._

lines.speaker: DULL
lines.text: Me, an’t shall please you; I am Antony Dull.
[_Reads_.]

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: _For Jaquenetta, so is the weaker vessel called which I

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: apprehended with the aforesaid swain, I keep her as a vessel of thy

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: law’s fury, and shall, at the least of thy sweet notice, bring her to

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: trial. Thine, in all compliments of devoted and heartburning heat of

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: duty,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Don Adriano de Armado._

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: This is not so well as I looked for, but the best that ever I heard.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Ay, the best for the worst. But, sirrah, what say you to this?

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: Sir, I confess the wench.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Did you hear the proclamation?

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: I do confess much of the hearing it, but little of the marking of it.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: It was proclaimed a year’s imprisonment to be taken with a wench.

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: I was taken with none, sir. I was taken with a damsel.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Well, it was proclaimed “damsel”.

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: This was no damsel neither, sir; she was a virgin.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: It is so varied too, for it was proclaimed “virgin”.

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: If it were, I deny her virginity. I was taken with a maid.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: This maid will not serve your turn, sir.

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: This maid will serve my turn, sir.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Sir, I will pronounce your sentence: you shall fast a week with bran

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: and water.

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: I had rather pray a month with mutton and porridge.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: And Don Armado shall be your keeper.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: My Lord Berowne, see him delivered o’er;

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: And go we, lords, to put in practice that

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Which each to other hath so strongly sworn.
[_Exeunt King, Longaville and Dumaine._]

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: I’ll lay my head to any good man’s hat

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: These oaths and laws will prove an idle scorn.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Sirrah, come on.

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: I suffer for the truth, sir; for true it is I was taken with

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: Jaquenetta, and Jaquenetta is a true girl. And therefore welcome the

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: sour cup of prosperity! Affliction may one day smile again, and till

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: then, sit thee down, sorrow.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Armado and Moth, his Page.

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: Boy, what sign is it when a man of great spirit grows melancholy?

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: A great sign, sir, that he will look sad.

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: Why, sadness is one and the selfsame thing, dear imp.

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: No, no, O Lord, sir, no.

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: How canst thou part sadness and melancholy, my tender juvenal?

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: By a familiar demonstration of the working, my tough signior.

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: Why tough signior? Why tough signior?

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: Why tender juvenal? Why tender juvenal?

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: I spoke it, tender juvenal, as a congruent epitheton appertaining to

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: thy young days, which we may nominate tender.

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: And I, tough signior, as an appertinent title to your old time, which

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: we may name tough.

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: Pretty and apt.

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: How mean you, sir? I pretty and my saying apt, or I apt, and my saying

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: pretty?

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: Thou pretty, because little.

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: Little pretty, because little. Wherefore apt?

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: And therefore apt, because quick.

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: Speak you this in my praise, master?

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: In thy condign praise.

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: I will praise an eel with the same praise.

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: What, that an eel is ingenious?

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: That an eel is quick.

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: I do say thou art quick in answers. Thou heat’st my blood.

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: I am answered, sir.

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: I love not to be crossed.
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: He speaks the mere contrary; crosses love not him.

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: I have promised to study three years with the Duke.

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: You may do it in an hour, sir.

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: Impossible.

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: How many is one thrice told?

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: I am ill at reckoning. It fitteth the spirit of a tapster.

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: You are a gentleman and a gamester, sir.

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: I confess both. They are both the varnish of a complete man.

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: Then I am sure you know how much the gross sum of deuce-ace amounts to.

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: It doth amount to one more than two.

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: Which the base vulgar do call three.

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: True.

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: Why, sir, is this such a piece of study? Now here’s three studied ere

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: ye’ll thrice wink. And how easy it is to put “years” to the word

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: “three”, and study three years in two words, the dancing horse will

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: tell you.

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: A most fine figure!
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: To prove you a cipher.

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: I will hereupon confess I am in love; and as it is base for a soldier

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: to love, so am I in love with a base wench. If drawing my sword against

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: the humour of affection would deliver me from the reprobate thought of

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: it, I would take desire prisoner, and ransom him to any French courtier

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: for a new-devised curtsy. I think scorn to sigh; methinks I should

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: outswear Cupid. Comfort me, boy. What great men have been in love?

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: Hercules, master.

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: Most sweet Hercules! More authority, dear boy, name more; and, sweet my

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: child, let them be men of good repute and carriage.

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: Samson, master. He was a man of good carriage, great carriage, for he

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: carried the town gates on his back like a porter, and he was in love.

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: O well-knit Samson, strong-jointed Samson! I do excel thee in my rapier

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: as much as thou didst me in carrying gates. I am in love too. Who was

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: Samson’s love, my dear Moth?

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: A woman, master.

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: Of what complexion?

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: Of all the four, or the three, or the two, or one of the four.

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: Tell me precisely of what complexion.

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: Of the sea-water green, sir.

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: Is that one of the four complexions?

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: As I have read, sir; and the best of them too.

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: Green indeed is the colour of lovers. But to have a love of that

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: colour, methinks Samson had small reason for it. He surely affected her

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: for her wit.

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: It was so, sir, for she had a green wit.

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: My love is most immaculate white and red.

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: Most maculate thoughts, master, are masked under such colours.

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: Define, define, well-educated infant.

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: My father’s wit and my mother’s tongue assist me!

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: Sweet invocation of a child, most pretty, and pathetical!

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: If she be made of white and red,

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: Her faults will ne’er be known;

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: For blushing cheeks by faults are bred,

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: And fears by pale white shown.

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: Then if she fear, or be to blame,

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: By this you shall not know,

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: For still her cheeks possess the same

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: Which native she doth owe.

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: A dangerous rhyme, master, against the reason of white and red.

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: Is there not a ballad, boy, of the King and the Beggar?

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: The world was very guilty of such a ballad some three ages since, but I

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: think now ’tis not to be found; or if it were, it would neither serve

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: for the writing nor the tune.

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: I will have that subject newly writ o’er, that I may example my

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: digression by some mighty precedent. Boy, I do love that country girl

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: that I took in the park with the rational hind Costard. She deserves

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: well.
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: To be whipped: and yet a better love than my master.

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: Sing, boy. My spirit grows heavy in love.

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: And that’s great marvel, loving a light wench.

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: I say, sing.

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: Forbear till this company be past.
Enter Costard the Clown, Dull the Constable and Jaquenetta a Wench.

lines.speaker: DULL
lines.text: Sir, the Duke’s pleasure is that you keep Costard safe; and you must

lines.speaker: DULL
lines.text: suffer him to take no delight, nor no penance, but he must fast three

lines.speaker: DULL
lines.text: days a week. For this damsel, I must keep her at the park. She is

lines.speaker: DULL
lines.text: allowed for the dey-woman. Fare you well.

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: I do betray myself with blushing.—Maid.

lines.speaker: JAQUENETTA
lines.text: Man.

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: I will visit thee at the lodge.

lines.speaker: JAQUENETTA
lines.text: That’s hereby.

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: I know where it is situate.

lines.speaker: JAQUENETTA
lines.text: Lord, how wise you are!

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: I will tell thee wonders.

lines.speaker: JAQUENETTA
lines.text: With that face?

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: I love thee.

lines.speaker: JAQUENETTA
lines.text: So I heard you say.

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: And so, farewell.

lines.speaker: JAQUENETTA
lines.text: Fair weather after you!

lines.speaker: DULL
lines.text: Come, Jaquenetta, away.
[_Exeunt Dull and Jaquenetta._]

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: Villain, thou shalt fast for thy offences ere thou be pardoned.

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: Well, sir, I hope when I do it I shall do it on a full stomach.

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: Thou shalt be heavily punished.

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: I am more bound to you than your fellows, for they are but lightly

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: rewarded.

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: Take away this villain. Shut him up.

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: Come, you transgressing slave, away!

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: Let me not be pent up, sir. I will fast being loose.

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: No, sir, that were fast and loose. Thou shalt to prison.

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: Well, if ever I do see the merry days of desolation that I have seen,

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: some shall see.

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: What shall some see?

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: Nay, nothing, Master Moth, but what they look upon. It is not for

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: prisoners to be too silent in their words, and therefore I will say

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: nothing. I thank God I have as little patience as another man, and

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: therefore I can be quiet.
[_Exeunt Moth and Costard._]

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: I do affect the very ground, which is base, where her shoe, which is

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: baser, guided by her foot, which is basest, doth tread. I shall be

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: forsworn, which is a great argument of falsehood, if I love. And how

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: can that be true love which is falsely attempted? Love is a familiar;

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: Love is a devil. There is no evil angel but Love. Yet was Samson so

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: tempted, and he had an excellent strength; yet was Solomon so seduced,

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: and he had a very good wit. Cupid’s butt-shaft is too hard for

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: Hercules’ club, and therefore too much odds for a Spaniard’s rapier.

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: The first and second cause will not serve my turn; the _passado_ he

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: respects not, the _duello_ he regards not. His disgrace is to be called

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: boy, but his glory is to subdue men. Adieu, valour; rust, rapier; be

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: still, drum, for your manager is in love. Yea, he loveth. Assist me,

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: some extemporal god of rhyme, for I am sure I shall turn sonnet.

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: Devise, wit; write, pen; for I am for whole volumes in folio.
[_Exit._]

scenes.setting: The King of Navarre’s park. A pavilion and tents at a distance

lines.text: Enter the Princess of France, with three attending Ladies: Rosaline, Maria, Katharine and three Lords: Boyet, and two others.

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: Now, madam, summon up your dearest spirits.

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: Consider who the King your father sends,

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: To whom he sends, and what’s his embassy.

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: Yourself, held precious in the world’s esteem,

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: To parley with the sole inheritor

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: Of all perfections that a man may owe,

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: Matchless Navarre; the plea of no less weight

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: Than Aquitaine, a dowry for a queen.

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: Be now as prodigal of all dear grace

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: As Nature was in making graces dear

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: When she did starve the general world beside

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: And prodigally gave them all to you.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Good Lord Boyet, my beauty, though but mean,

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Needs not the painted flourish of your praise.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Beauty is bought by judgement of the eye,

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Not uttered by base sale of chapmen’s tongues.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: I am less proud to hear you tell my worth

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Than you much willing to be counted wise

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: In spending your wit in the praise of mine.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: But now to task the tasker: good Boyet,

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: You are not ignorant, all-telling fame

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Doth noise abroad Navarre hath made a vow,

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Till painful study shall outwear three years,

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: No woman may approach his silent court.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Therefore to’s seemeth it a needful course,

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Before we enter his forbidden gates,

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: To know his pleasure; and in that behalf,

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Bold of your worthiness, we single you

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: As our best-moving fair solicitor.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Tell him the daughter of the King of France,

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: On serious business craving quick dispatch,

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Importunes personal conference with his Grace.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Haste, signify so much, while we attend,

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Like humble-visaged suitors, his high will.

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: Proud of employment, willingly I go.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: All pride is willing pride, and yours is so.
[_Exit Boyet._]

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Who are the votaries, my loving lords,

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: That are vow-fellows with this virtuous Duke?

lines.speaker: LORD
lines.text: Lord Longaville is one.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Know you the man?

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: I know him, madam. At a marriage feast

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: Between Lord Perigort and the beauteous heir

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: Of Jaques Falconbridge, solemnized

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: In Normandy, saw I this Longaville.

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: A man of sovereign parts, he is esteemed,

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: Well fitted in arts, glorious in arms.

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: Nothing becomes him ill that he would well.

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: The only soil of his fair virtue’s gloss,

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: If virtue’s gloss will stain with any soil,

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: Is a sharp wit matched with too blunt a will,

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: Whose edge hath power to cut, whose will still wills

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: It should none spare that come within his power.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Some merry mocking lord, belike. Is’t so?

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: They say so most that most his humours know.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Such short-lived wits do wither as they grow.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Who are the rest?

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: The young Dumaine, a well-accomplished youth,

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: Of all that virtue love for virtue loved;

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: Most power to do most harm, least knowing ill,

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: For he hath wit to make an ill shape good,

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: And shape to win grace though he had no wit.

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: I saw him at the Duke Alençon’s once;

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: And much too little of that good I saw

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: Is my report to his great worthiness.

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: Another of these students at that time

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: Was there with him, if I have heard a truth.

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: Berowne they call him, but a merrier man,

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: Within the limit of becoming mirth,

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: I never spent an hour’s talk withal.

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: His eye begets occasion for his wit,

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: For every object that the one doth catch

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: The other turns to a mirth-moving jest,

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: Which his fair tongue, conceit’s expositor,

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: Delivers in such apt and gracious words

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: That aged ears play truant at his tales,

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: And younger hearings are quite ravished,

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: So sweet and voluble is his discourse.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: God bless my ladies! Are they all in love,

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: That every one her own hath garnished

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: With such bedecking ornaments of praise?

lines.speaker: LORD
lines.text: Here comes Boyet.
Enter Boyet.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Now, what admittance, lord?

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: Navarre had notice of your fair approach,

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: And he and his competitors in oath

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: Were all addressed to meet you, gentle lady,

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: Before I came. Marry, thus much I have learned:

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: He rather means to lodge you in the field,

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: Like one that comes here to besiege his court,

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: Than seek a dispensation for his oath,

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: To let you enter his unpeopled house.
Enter King of Navarre, Longaville, Dumaine, Berowne and Attendants.

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: Here comes Navarre.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Fair Princess, welcome to the court of Navarre.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: “Fair” I give you back again, and “welcome” I have not yet. The roof of

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: this court is too high to be yours, and welcome to the wide fields too

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: base to be mine.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: You shall be welcome, madam, to my court.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: I will be welcome then. Conduct me thither.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Hear me, dear lady. I have sworn an oath.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Our Lady help my lord! He’ll be forsworn.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Not for the world, fair madam, by my will.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Why, will shall break it; will, and nothing else.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Your ladyship is ignorant what it is.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Were my lord so, his ignorance were wise,

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Where now his knowledge must prove ignorance.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: I hear your Grace hath sworn out housekeeping.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: ’Tis deadly sin to keep that oath, my lord,

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: And sin to break it.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: But pardon me, I am too sudden bold.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: To teach a teacher ill beseemeth me.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Vouchsafe to read the purpose of my coming,

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: And suddenly resolve me in my suit.
[_She gives him a paper._]

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Madam, I will, if suddenly I may.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: You will the sooner that I were away,

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: For you’ll prove perjured if you make me stay.
[_The King reads the paper._]
[_To Rosaline_.]

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Did not I dance with you in Brabant once?

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: Did not I dance with you in Brabant once?

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: I know you did.

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: How needless was it then

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: To ask the question!

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: You must not be so quick.

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: ’Tis long of you that spur me with such questions.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Your wit’s too hot, it speeds too fast, ’twill tire.

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: Not till it leave the rider in the mire.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: What time o’ day?

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: The hour that fools should ask.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Now fair befall your mask.

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: Fair fall the face it covers.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: And send you many lovers!

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: Amen, so you be none.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Nay, then will I be gone.

lines.text: Madam, your father here doth intimate

lines.text: But say that he or we, as neither have,

lines.speaker: KING

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: If then the King your father will restore

lines.text: But that one half which is unsatisfied,

lines.speaker: KING

lines.speaker: KING

lines.speaker: KING

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Dear Princess, were not his requests so far

lines.text: From reason’s yielding, your fair self should make

lines.text: A yielding ’gainst some reason in my breast,

lines.text: And go well satisfied to France again.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: You do the King my father too much wrong,

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: And wrong the reputation of your name,

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: In so unseeming to confess receipt

lines.speaker: PRINCESS

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: And, if you prove it, I’ll repay it back

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Then, forester, my friend, where is the bush

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: That we must stand and play the murderer in?

lines.speaker: FORESTER
lines.text: Hereby, upon the edge of yonder coppice,

lines.speaker: FORESTER
lines.text: A stand where you may make “the fairest shoot”.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: I thank my beauty, I am fair that shoot,

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: And thereupon thou speak’st the fairest shoot.

lines.speaker: FORESTER
lines.text: Pardon me, madam, for I meant not so.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: What, what? First praise me, and again say no?

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: O short-lived pride! Not fair? Alack for woe!

lines.speaker: FORESTER
lines.text: Yes, madam, fair.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Nay, never paint me now.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Where fair is not, praise cannot mend the brow.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Here, good my glass, take this for telling true:
[_She gives him money._]

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Fair payment for foul words is more than due.

lines.speaker: FORESTER
lines.text: Nothing but fair is that which you inherit.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: See, see, my beauty will be saved by merit.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: O heresy in fair, fit for these days!

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: A giving hand, though foul, shall have fair praise.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: But come, the bow. Now mercy goes to kill,

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: And shooting well is then accounted ill.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Thus will I save my credit in the shoot:

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Not wounding, pity would not let me do’t;

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: If wounding, then it was to show my skill,

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: That more for praise than purpose meant to kill.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: And out of question so it is sometimes,

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Glory grows guilty of detested crimes,

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: When, for fame’s sake, for praise, an outward part,

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: We bend to that the working of the heart;

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: As I for praise alone now seek to spill

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: The poor deer’s blood, that my heart means no ill.

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: Do not curst wives hold that self-sovereignty

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: Only for praise’ sake, when they strive to be

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: Lords o’er their lords?

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Only for praise; and praise we may afford

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: To any lady that subdues a lord.
Enter Costard.

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: Here comes a member of the commonwealth.

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: God dig-you-den all! Pray you, which is the head lady?

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Thou shalt know her, fellow, by the rest that have no heads.

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: Which is the greatest lady, the highest?

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: The thickest and the tallest.

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: The thickest and the tallest. It is so, truth is truth.

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: An your waist, mistress, were as slender as my wit,

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: One o’ these maids’ girdles for your waist should be fit.

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: Are not you the chief woman? You are the thickest here.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: What’s your will, sir? What’s your will?

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: I have a letter from Monsieur Berowne to one Lady Rosaline.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: O, thy letter, thy letter! He’s a good friend of mine.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Stand aside, good bearer. Boyet, you can carve.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Break up this capon.

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: I am bound to serve.

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: This letter is mistook; it importeth none here.

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: It is writ to Jaquenetta.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: We will read it, I swear.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Break the neck of the wax, and everyone give ear.
[_Reads_.]

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: _By heaven, that thou art fair is most infallible; true that

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: thou art beauteous; truth itself that thou art lovely. More fairer than

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: fair, beautiful than beauteous, truer than truth itself, have

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: commiseration on thy heroical vassal. The magnanimous and most

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: illustrate King Cophetua set eye upon the pernicious and indubitate

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: beggar Zenelophon, and he it was that might rightly say,_ “Veni, vidi,

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: vici,” _which to annothanize in the vulgar—O base and obscure

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: vulgar!_—videlicet, _He came, see, and overcame. He came, one; see,

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: two; overcame, three. Who came? The King. Why did he come? To see. Why

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: did he see? To overcome. To whom came he? To the beggar. What saw he?

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: The beggar. Who overcame he? The beggar. The conclusion is victory. On

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: whose side? The King’s. The captive is enriched. On whose side? The

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: beggar’s. The catastrophe is a nuptial. On whose side? The King’s? No,

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: on both in one, or one in both. I am the King, for so stands the

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: comparison; thou the beggar, for so witnesseth thy lowliness. Shall I

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: command thy love? I may. Shall I enforce thy love? I could. Shall I

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: entreat thy love? I will. What shalt thou exchange for rags? Robes. For

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: tittles? Titles. For thyself? Me. Thus expecting thy reply, I profane

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: my lips on thy foot, my eyes on thy picture, and my heart on thy every

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: part.

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: Thine in the dearest design of industry,

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: Don Adriano de Armado.

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: Thus dost thou hear the Nemean lion roar

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: ’Gainst thee, thou lamb, that standest as his prey.

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: Submissive fall his princely feet before,

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: And he from forage will incline to play.

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: But if thou strive, poor soul, what are thou then?

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: Food for his rage, repasture for his den._

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: What plume of feathers is he that indited this letter?

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: What vane? What weathercock? Did you ever hear better?

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: I am much deceived but I remember the style.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Else your memory is bad, going o’er it erewhile.

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: This Armado is a Spaniard that keeps here in court,

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: A phantasime, a Monarcho, and one that makes sport

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: To the Prince and his book-mates.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Thou, fellow, a word.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Who gave thee this letter?

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: I told you: my lord.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: To whom shouldst thou give it?

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: From my lord to my lady.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: From which lord to which lady?

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: From my Lord Berowne, a good master of mine,

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: To a lady of France that he called Rosaline.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Thou hast mistaken his letter. Come, lords, away.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Here, sweet, put up this: ’twill be thine another day.
[_Exeunt all but Boyet, Rosaline, Maria and Costard._]

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: Who is the shooter? Who is the shooter?

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: Shall I teach you to know?

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: Ay, my continent of beauty.

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: Why, she that bears the bow.

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: Finely put off!

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: My lady goes to kill horns, but if thou marry,

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: Hang me by the neck if horns that year miscarry.

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: Finely put on!

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: Well, then, I am the shooter.

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: And who is your deer?

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: If we choose by the horns, yourself come not near.

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: Finely put on indeed!

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: You still wrangle with her, Boyet, and she strikes at the brow.

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: But she herself is hit lower. Have I hit her now?

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: Shall I come upon thee with an old saying, that was a man when King

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: Pepin of France was a little boy, as touching the hit it?

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: So I may answer thee with one as old, that was a woman when Queen

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: Guinevere of Britain was a little wench, as touching the hit it.

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: Thou canst not hit it, hit it, hit it,

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: Thou canst not hit it, my good man.

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: An I cannot, cannot, cannot,

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: An I cannot, another can.
[_Exeunt Rosaline._]

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: By my troth, most pleasant. How both did fit it!

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: A mark marvellous well shot, for they both did hit it.

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: A mark! O, mark but that mark! A mark, says my lady!

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: Let the mark have a prick in’t, to mete at, if it may be.

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: Wide o’ the bow hand! I’ faith, your hand is out.

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: Indeed, a’ must shoot nearer, or he’ll ne’er hit the clout.

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: An if my hand be out, then belike your hand is in.

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: Then will she get the upshoot by cleaving the pin.

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: Come, come, you talk greasily, your lips grow foul.

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: She’s too hard for you at pricks, sir. Challenge her to bowl.

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: I fear too much rubbing. Good night, my good owl.
[_Exeunt Boyet and Maria._]

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: By my soul, a swain, a most simple clown!

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: Lord, Lord, how the ladies and I have put him down!

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: O’ my troth, most sweet jests, most incony vulgar wit,

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: When it comes so smoothly off, so obscenely, as it were, so fit.

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: Armado, o’ the one side, O, a most dainty man!

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: To see him walk before a lady and to bear her fan!

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: To see him kiss his hand and how most sweetly he will swear!

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: And his page o’ t’other side, that handful of wit!

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: Ah, heavens, it is a most pathetical nit.
[_Shout within._]

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: Sola, sola!
[_Exit._]
Enter Dull, Holofernes, the Pedant and Nathaniel.

lines.speaker: NATHANIEL
lines.text: Very reverend sport, truly, and done in the testimony of a good

lines.speaker: NATHANIEL
lines.text: conscience.

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: The deer was, as you know, _sanguis_, in blood, ripe as the pomewater,

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: who now hangeth like a jewel in the ear of _caelo_, the sky, the

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: welkin, the heaven, and anon falleth like a crab on the face of

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: _terra_, the soil, the land, the earth.

lines.speaker: NATHANIEL
lines.text: Truly, Master Holofernes, the epithets are sweetly varied, like a

lines.speaker: NATHANIEL
lines.text: scholar at the least. But, sir, I assure ye it was a buck of the first

lines.speaker: NATHANIEL
lines.text: head.

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: Sir Nathaniel, _haud credo_.

lines.speaker: DULL
lines.text: ’Twas not a “auld grey doe”, ’twas a pricket.

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: Most barbarous intimation! Yet a kind of insinuation, as it were, _in

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: via_, in way, of explication; _facere_, as it were, replication, or

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: rather, _ostentare_, to show, as it were, his inclination, after his

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: undressed, unpolished, uneducated, unpruned, untrained, or rather,

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: unlettered, or ratherest, unconfirmed fashion, to insert again my _haud

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: credo_ for a deer.

lines.speaker: DULL
lines.text: I said the deer was not a “auld grey doe”, ’twas a pricket.

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: Twice-sod simplicity, _bis coctus!_

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: O, thou monster Ignorance, how deformed dost thou look!

lines.speaker: NATHANIEL
lines.text: Sir, he hath never fed of the dainties that are bred of a book.

lines.speaker: NATHANIEL
lines.text: He hath not eat paper, as it were; he hath not drunk ink.

lines.speaker: NATHANIEL
lines.text: His intellect is not replenished; he is only an animal, only sensible

lines.speaker: NATHANIEL
lines.text: in the duller parts.

lines.speaker: NATHANIEL
lines.text: And such barren plants are set before us that we thankful should be—

lines.speaker: NATHANIEL
lines.text: Which we of taste and feeling are—for those parts that do fructify in

lines.speaker: NATHANIEL
lines.text: us more than he.

lines.speaker: NATHANIEL
lines.text: For as it would ill become me to be vain, indiscreet, or a fool,

lines.speaker: NATHANIEL
lines.text: So, were there a patch set on learning, to see him in a school.

lines.speaker: NATHANIEL
lines.text: But, _omne bene_, say I, being of an old father’s mind;

lines.speaker: NATHANIEL
lines.text: Many can brook the weather that love not the wind.

lines.speaker: DULL
lines.text: You two are bookmen. Can you tell me by your wit

lines.speaker: DULL
lines.text: What was a month old at Cain’s birth, that’s not five weeks old as yet?

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: Dictynna, goodman Dull. Dictynna, goodman Dull.

lines.speaker: DULL
lines.text: What is Dictynna?

lines.speaker: NATHANIEL
lines.text: A title to Phoebe, to Luna, to the moon.

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: The moon was a month old when Adam was no more,

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: And raught not to five weeks when he came to five-score.

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: Th’ allusion holds in the exchange.

lines.speaker: DULL
lines.text: ’Tis true, indeed. The collusion holds in the exchange.

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: God comfort thy capacity! I say, th’ allusion holds in the exchange.

lines.speaker: DULL
lines.text: And I say the pollution holds in the exchange, for the moon is never

lines.speaker: DULL
lines.text: but a month old; and I say beside that ’twas a pricket that the

lines.speaker: DULL
lines.text: Princess killed.

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: Sir Nathaniel, will you hear an extemporal epitaph on the death of the

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: deer? And, to humour the ignorant, call I the deer the Princess killed

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: a pricket.

lines.speaker: NATHANIEL
lines.text: _Perge_, good Master Holofernes, _perge_, so it shall please you to

lines.speaker: NATHANIEL
lines.text: abrogate scurrility.

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: I will something affect the letter; for it argues facility.

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: The preyful Princess pierced and pricked a pretty pleasing pricket;

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: Some say a sore; but not a sore till now made sore with shooting.

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: The dogs did yell, put “l” to sore, then sorel jumps from thicket;

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: Or pricket sore, or else sorel, the people fall a-hooting.

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: If sore be sore, then “L” to “sore” makes fifty sores o’ sorel.

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: Of one sore I an hundred make, by adding but one more “L”.

lines.speaker: NATHANIEL
lines.text: A rare talent!
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: DULL
lines.text: If a talent be a claw, look how he claws him with a talent.

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: This is a gift that I have, simple, simple; a foolish extravagant

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: spirit, full of forms, figures, shapes, objects, ideas, apprehensions,

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: motions, revolutions. These are begot in the ventricle of memory,

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: nourished in the womb of _pia mater_, and delivered upon the mellowing

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: of occasion. But the gift is good in those in whom it is acute, and I

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: am thankful for it.

lines.speaker: NATHANIEL
lines.text: Sir, I praise the Lord for you, and so may my parishioners, for their

lines.speaker: NATHANIEL
lines.text: sons are well tutored by you, and their daughters profit very greatly

lines.speaker: NATHANIEL
lines.text: under you. You are a good member of the commonwealth.

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: _Mehercle!_ If their sons be ingenious, they shall want no instruction;

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: if their daughters be capable, I will put it to them. But, _vir sapit

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: qui pauca loquitur_. A soul feminine saluteth us.
Enter Jaquenetta and Costard.

lines.speaker: JAQUENETTA
lines.text: God give you good morrow, Master Person.

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: Master Person, _quasi_ pierce one. And if one should be pierced, which

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: is the one?

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: Marry, Master schoolmaster, he that is likest to a hogshead.

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: Of piercing a hogshead! A good lustre or conceit in a turf of earth;

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: fire enough for a flint, pearl enough for a swine. ’Tis pretty; it is

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: well.

lines.speaker: JAQUENETTA
lines.text: Good Master Parson, be so good as read me this letter. It was given me

lines.speaker: JAQUENETTA
lines.text: by Costard, and sent me from Don Armado. I beseech you read it.
[_Giving a letter to Nathaniel._]

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: _Fauste precor, gelida quando pecus omne sub umbra Ruminat_—

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: and so forth. Ah, good old Mantuan, I may speak of thee as the

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: traveller doth of Venice:

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: _Venetia, Venetia,

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: Chi non ti vede, non ti pretia._

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: Old Mantuan, old Mantuan! Who understandeth thee not, loves thee not.
[_He sings_.]

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: Ut, re, sol, la, mi, fa.

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: Under pardon, sir, what are the contents? Or rather as Horace says in

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: his—What, my soul, verses?

lines.speaker: NATHANIEL
lines.text: Ay, sir, and very learned.

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: Let me hear a staff, a stanze, a verse,

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: _Lege, domine_.
[_Reads_.]

lines.speaker: NATHANIEL
lines.text: _If love make me forsworn, how shall I swear to love?

lines.speaker: NATHANIEL
lines.text: Ah, never faith could hold, if not to beauty vowed.

lines.speaker: NATHANIEL
lines.text: Though to myself forsworn, to thee I’ll faithful prove.

lines.speaker: NATHANIEL
lines.text: Those thoughts to me were oaks, to thee like osiers bowed.

lines.speaker: NATHANIEL
lines.text: Study his bias leaves, and makes his book thine eyes,

lines.speaker: NATHANIEL
lines.text: Where all those pleasures live that art would comprehend.

lines.speaker: NATHANIEL
lines.text: If knowledge be the mark, to know thee shall suffice.

lines.speaker: NATHANIEL
lines.text: Well learned is that tongue that well can thee commend,

lines.speaker: NATHANIEL
lines.text: All ignorant that soul that sees thee without wonder;

lines.speaker: NATHANIEL
lines.text: Which is to me some praise, that I thy parts admire.

lines.speaker: NATHANIEL
lines.text: Thy eye Jove’s lightning bears, thy voice his dreadful thunder,

lines.speaker: NATHANIEL
lines.text: Which, not to anger bent, is music and sweet fire.

lines.speaker: NATHANIEL
lines.text: Celestial as thou art, O, pardon love this wrong,

lines.speaker: NATHANIEL
lines.text: That sings heaven’s praise with such an earthly tongue._

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: You find not the apostrophus, and so miss the accent. Let me supervise

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: the canzonet. [_He takes the letter_.] Here are only numbers ratified,

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: but, for the elegancy, facility, and golden cadence of poesy, _caret_.

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: Ovidius Naso was the man. And why indeed “Naso,” but for smelling out

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: the odoriferous flowers of fancy, the jerks of invention? _Imitari_ is

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: nothing: so doth the hound his master, the ape his keeper, the tired

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: horse his rider. But, damosella virgin, was this directed to you?

lines.speaker: JAQUENETTA
lines.text: Ay, sir, from one Monsieur Berowne, one of the strange queen’s lords.

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: I will overglance the superscript: _To the snow-white hand of the most

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: beauteous Lady Rosaline._ I will look again on the intellect of the

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: letter, for the nomination of the party writing to the person written

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: unto: _Your Ladyship’s in all desired employment, Berowne._ Sir

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: Nathaniel, this Berowne is one of the votaries with the King, and here

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: he hath framed a letter to a sequent of the stranger queen’s, which

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: accidentally, or by the way of progression, hath miscarried. Trip and

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
