lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Her favour turns the fashion of the days,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: For native blood is counted painting now;

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: And therefore red, that would avoid dispraise,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Paints itself black, to imitate her brow.

lines.speaker: DUMAINE
lines.text: To look like her are chimney-sweepers black.

lines.speaker: LONGAVILLE
lines.text: And since her time are colliers counted bright.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: And Ethiopes of their sweet complexion crack.

lines.speaker: DUMAINE
lines.text: Dark needs no candles now, for dark is light.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Your mistresses dare never come in rain,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: For fear their colours should be washed away.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: ’Twere good yours did; for, sir, to tell you plain,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: I’ll find a fairer face not washed today.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: I’ll prove her fair, or talk till doomsday here.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: No devil will fright thee then so much as she.

lines.speaker: DUMAINE
lines.text: I never knew man hold vile stuff so dear.
[_Showing his shoe_.]

lines.speaker: LONGAVILLE
lines.text: Look, here’s thy love, my foot and her face see.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: O, if the streets were paved with thine eyes,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Her feet were much too dainty for such tread.

lines.speaker: DUMAINE
lines.text: O vile! Then, as she goes, what upward lies

lines.speaker: DUMAINE
lines.text: The street should see as she walked over head.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: But what of this? Are we not all in love?

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Nothing so sure, and thereby all forsworn.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Then leave this chat, and, good Berowne, now prove

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Our loving lawful, and our faith not torn.

lines.speaker: DUMAINE
lines.text: Ay, marry, there; some flattery for this evil.

lines.speaker: LONGAVILLE
lines.text: O, some authority how to proceed.

lines.speaker: LONGAVILLE
lines.text: Some tricks, some quillets, how to cheat the devil.

lines.speaker: DUMAINE
lines.text: Some salve for perjury.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: O, ’tis more than need.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Have at you, then, affection’s men-at-arms.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Consider what you first did swear unto:

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: To fast, to study, and to see no woman—

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Flat treason ’gainst the kingly state of youth.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Say, can you fast? Your stomachs are too young,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: And abstinence engenders maladies.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: O, we have made a vow to study, lords,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: And in that vow we have forsworn our books;

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: For when would you, my liege, or you, or you,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: In leaden contemplation have found out

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Such fiery numbers as the prompting eyes

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Of beauty’s tutors have enriched you with?

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Other slow arts entirely keep the brain,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: And therefore, finding barren practisers,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Scarce show a harvest of their heavy toil;

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: But love, first learned in a lady’s eyes,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Lives not alone immured in the brain,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: But with the motion of all elements

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Courses as swift as thought in every power,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: And gives to every power a double power,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Above their functions and their offices.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: It adds a precious seeing to the eye.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: A lover’s eyes will gaze an eagle blind.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: A lover’s ear will hear the lowest sound,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: When the suspicious head of theft is stopped.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Love’s feeling is more soft and sensible

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Than are the tender horns of cockled snails.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Love’s tongue proves dainty Bacchus gross in taste.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: For valour, is not Love a Hercules,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Still climbing trees in the Hesperides?

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Subtle as Sphinx, as sweet and musical

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: As bright Apollo’s lute, strung with his hair.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: And when Love speaks, the voice of all the gods

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Make heaven drowsy with the harmony.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Never durst poet touch a pen to write

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Until his ink were tempered with Love’s sighs.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: O, then his lines would ravish savage ears

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: And plant in tyrants mild humility.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: From women’s eyes this doctrine I derive.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: They sparkle still the right Promethean fire;

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: They are the books, the arts, the academes,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: That show, contain, and nourish, all the world;

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Else none at all in aught proves excellent.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Then fools you were these women to forswear,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Or, keeping what is sworn, you will prove fools.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: For wisdom’s sake, a word that all men love,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Or for love’s sake, a word that loves all men,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Or for men’s sake, the authors of these women,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Or women’s sake, by whom we men are men,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Let us once lose our oaths to find ourselves,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Or else we lose ourselves to keep our oaths.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: It is religion to be thus forsworn,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: For charity itself fulfils the law,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: And who can sever love from charity?

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Saint Cupid, then, and, soldiers, to the field!

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Advance your standards, and upon them, lords!

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Pell-mell, down with them! But be first advised

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: In conflict that you get the sun of them.

lines.speaker: LONGAVILLE
lines.text: Now to plain dealing. Lay these glozes by.

lines.speaker: LONGAVILLE
lines.text: Shall we resolve to woo these girls of France?

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: And win them too. Therefore let us devise

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Some entertainment for them in their tents.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: First, from the park let us conduct them thither.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Then homeward every man attach the hand

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Of his fair mistress. In the afternoon

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: We will with some strange pastime solace them,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Such as the shortness of the time can shape;

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: For revels, dances, masques, and merry hours

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Forerun fair Love, strewing her way with flowers.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Away, away! No time shall be omitted

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: That will betime and may by us be fitted.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: _Allons! allons!_ Sowed cockle reaped no corn,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: And justice always whirls in equal measure.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Light wenches may prove plagues to men forsworn;

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: If so, our copper buys no better treasure.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Holofernes, Sir Nathaniel and Dull.

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: _Satis quod sufficit._

lines.speaker: NATHANIEL
lines.text: I praise God for you, sir. Your reasons at dinner have been sharp and

lines.speaker: NATHANIEL
lines.text: sententious, pleasant without scurrility, witty without affection,

lines.speaker: NATHANIEL
lines.text: audacious without impudency, learned without opinion, and strange

lines.speaker: NATHANIEL
lines.text: without heresy. I did converse this _quondam_ day with a companion of

lines.speaker: NATHANIEL
lines.text: the King’s, who is intituled, nominated, or called, Don Adriano de

lines.speaker: NATHANIEL
lines.text: Armado.

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: _Novi hominem tanquam te._ His humour is lofty, his discourse

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: peremptory, his tongue filed, his eye ambitious, his gait majestical

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: and his general behaviour vain, ridiculous, and thrasonical. He is too

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: picked, too spruce, too affected, too odd, as it were, too peregrinate,

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: as I may call it.

lines.speaker: NATHANIEL
lines.text: A most singular and choice epithet.
[_Draws out his table-book._]

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: He draweth out the thread of his verbosity finer than the staple of his

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: argument. I abhor such fanatical phantasimes, such insociable and

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: point-devise companions, such rackers of orthography, as to speak

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: “dout” _sine_ “b”, when he should say “doubt”, “det” when he should

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: pronounce “debt”—_d, e, b, t_, not _d, e, t_. He clepeth a calf “cauf”,

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: half “hauf”; neighbour _vocatur_ “nebour”, neigh abbreviated “ne”. This

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: is abhominable, which he would call “abominable”. It insinuateth me of

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: insanie. _Ne intelligis, domine?_ To make frantic, lunatic.

lines.speaker: NATHANIEL
lines.text: _Laus Deo, bone intelligo._

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: _Bone? Bone_ for _bene?_ Priscian a little scratched; ’twill serve.
Enter Armado, Moth and Costard.

lines.speaker: NATHANIEL
lines.text: _Videsne quis venit?_

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: _Video, et gaudeo._

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: _Chirrah!_

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: _Quare_ “chirrah”, not “sirrah”?

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: Men of peace, well encountered.

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: Most military sir, salutation.
[_Aside to Costard_.]

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: They have been at a great feast of languages and

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: stolen the scraps.

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: O, they have lived long on the almsbasket of words. I marvel thy master

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: hath not eaten thee for a word, for thou art not so long by the head as

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: _honorificabilitudinitatibus_. Thou art easier swallowed than a

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: flap-dragon.

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: Peace! The peal begins.
[_To Holofernes_.]

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: Monsieur, are you not lettered?

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: Yes, yes, he teaches boys the hornbook. What is _a, b_, spelt backward

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: with the horn on his head?

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: _Ba, pueritia_, with a horn added.

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: _Ba_, most silly sheep with a horn. You hear his learning.

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: _Quis, quis_, thou consonant?

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: The third of the five vowels, if you repeat them; or the fifth, if I.

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: I will repeat them: _a, e, i_—

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: The sheep. The other two concludes it: _o, u_.

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: Now, by the salt wave of the Mediterraneum, a sweet touch, a quick

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: venue of wit! Snip, snap, quick and home! It rejoiceth my intellect.

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: True wit!

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: Offered by a child to an old man—which is wit-old.

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: What is the figure? What is the figure?

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: Horns.

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: Thou disputes like an infant. Go whip thy gig.

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: Lend me your horn to make one, and I will whip about your infamy _unum

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: cita_. A gig of a cuckold’s horn.

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: An I had but one penny in the world, thou shouldst have it to buy

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: gingerbread. Hold, there is the very remuneration I had of thy master,

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: thou halfpenny purse of wit, thou pigeon-egg of discretion. O, an the

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: heavens were so pleased that thou wert but my bastard, what a joyful

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: father wouldst thou make me! Go to, thou hast it _ad dunghill_, at the

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: fingers’ ends, as they say.

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: O, I smell false Latin! _Dunghill_ for _unguem_.

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: Arts-man, preambulate. We will be singuled from the barbarous. Do you

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: not educate youth at the charge-house on the top of the mountain?

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: Or _mons_, the hill.

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: At your sweet pleasure, for the mountain.

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: I do, _sans question_.

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: Sir, it is the King’s most sweet pleasure and affection to congratulate

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: the Princess at her pavilion in the posteriors of this day, which the

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: rude multitude call the afternoon.

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: The posterior of the day, most generous sir, is liable, congruent, and

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: measurable for the afternoon. The word is well culled, chose, sweet,

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: and apt, I do assure you, sir, I do assure.

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: Sir, the King is a noble gentleman, and my familiar, I do assure ye,

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: very good friend. For what is inward between us, let it pass. I do

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: beseech thee, remember thy courtesy; I beseech thee, apparel thy head.

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: And among other importunate and most serious designs, and of great

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: import indeed, too—but let that pass. For I must tell thee it will

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: please his Grace, by the world, sometime to lean upon my poor shoulder

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: and with his royal finger thus dally with my excrement, with my

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: mustachio. But, sweet heart, let that pass. By the world, I recount no

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: fable! Some certain special honours it pleaseth his greatness to impart

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: to Armado, a soldier, a man of travel, that hath seen the world. But

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: let that pass. The very all of all is—but, sweet heart, I do implore

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: secrecy—that the King would have me present the Princess, sweet chuck,

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: with some delightful ostentation, or show, or pageant, or antic, or

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: firework. Now, understanding that the curate and your sweet self are

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: good at such eruptions and sudden breaking-out of mirth, as it were, I

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: have acquainted you withal, to the end to crave your assistance.

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: Sir, you shall present before her the Nine Worthies. Sir Nathaniel, as

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: concerning some entertainment of time, some show in the posterior of

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: this day, to be rendered by our assistance, the King’s command, and

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: this most gallant, illustrate, and learned gentleman, before the

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: Princess, I say, none so fit as to present the Nine Worthies.

lines.speaker: NATHANIEL
lines.text: Where will you find men worthy enough to present them?

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: Joshua, yourself; myself; and this gallant gentleman, Judas Maccabaeus.

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: This swain, because of his great limb or joint, shall pass Pompey the

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: Great; the page, Hercules.

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: Pardon, sir; error. He is not quantity enough for that Worthy’s thumb;

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: he is not so big as the end of his club.

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: Shall I have audience? He shall present Hercules in minority. His enter

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: and exit shall be strangling a snake; and I will have an apology for

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: that purpose.

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: An excellent device! So, if any of the audience hiss, you may cry “Well

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: done, Hercules, now thou crushest the snake!” That is the way to make

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: an offence gracious, though few have the grace to do it.

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: For the rest of the Worthies?

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: I will play three myself.

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: Thrice-worthy gentleman!

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: Shall I tell you a thing?

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: We attend.

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: We will have, if this fadge not, an antic. I beseech you, follow.

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: _Via_, goodman Dull! Thou has spoken no word all this while.

lines.speaker: DULL
lines.text: Nor understood none neither, sir.

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: _Allons!_ we will employ thee.

lines.speaker: DULL
lines.text: I’ll make one in a dance, or so; or I will play on the tabor to the

lines.speaker: DULL
lines.text: Worthies, and let them dance the hay.

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: Most dull, honest Dull! To our sport, away.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: The same. Before the Princess’s pavilion

lines.text: Enter the Princess, Rosaline, Katharine and Maria.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Sweet hearts, we shall be rich ere we depart,

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: If fairings come thus plentifully in.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: A lady walled about with diamonds!

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Look you what I have from the loving King.

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: Madam, came nothing else along with that?

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Nothing but this? Yes, as much love in rhyme

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: As would be crammed up in a sheet of paper

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Writ o’ both sides the leaf, margent and all,

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: That he was fain to seal on Cupid’s name.

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: That was the way to make his godhead wax,

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: For he hath been five thousand years a boy.

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: Ay, and a shrewd unhappy gallows too.

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: You’ll ne’er be friends with him. He killed your sister.

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: He made her melancholy, sad, and heavy;

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: And so she died. Had she been light, like you,

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: Of such a merry, nimble, stirring spirit,

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: She might ha’ been a grandam ere she died.

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: And so may you, for a light heart lives long.

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: What’s your dark meaning, mouse, of this light word?

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: A light condition in a beauty dark.

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: We need more light to find your meaning out.

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: You’ll mar the light by taking it in snuff;

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: Therefore I’ll darkly end the argument.

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: Look what you do, you do it still i’ th’ dark.

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: So do not you, for you are a light wench.

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: Indeed, I weigh not you, and therefore light.

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: You weigh me not? O, that’s you care not for me.

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: Great reason, for past cure is still past care.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Well bandied both; a set of wit well played.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: But, Rosaline, you have a favour too.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Who sent it? And what is it?

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: I would you knew.

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: An if my face were but as fair as yours,

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: My favour were as great. Be witness this.

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: Nay, I have verses too, I thank Berowne;

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: The numbers true, and, were the numbering too,

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: I were the fairest goddess on the ground.

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: I am compared to twenty thousand fairs.

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: O, he hath drawn my picture in his letter.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Anything like?

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: Much in the letters, nothing in the praise.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Beauteous as ink: a good conclusion.

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: Fair as a text B in a copy-book.

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: ’Ware pencils, how! Let me not die your debtor,

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: My red dominical, my golden letter.

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: O, that your face were not so full of O’s!

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: A pox of that jest! And beshrew all shrews.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: But, Katharine, what was sent to you from fair Dumaine?

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: Madam, this glove.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Did he not send you twain?

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: Yes, madam, and moreover,

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: Some thousand verses of a faithful lover.

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: A huge translation of hypocrisy,

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: Vilely compiled, profound simplicity.

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: This, and these pearls, to me sent Longaville.

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: The letter is too long by half a mile.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: I think no less. Dost thou not wish in heart

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: The chain were longer and the letter short?

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: Ay, or I would these hands might never part.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: We are wise girls to mock our lovers so.

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: They are worse fools to purchase mocking so.

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: That same Berowne I’ll torture ere I go.

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: O that I knew he were but in by th’ week!

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: How I would make him fawn, and beg, and seek,

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: And wait the season, and observe the times,

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: And spend his prodigal wits in bootless rhymes,

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: And shape his service wholly to my hests,

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: And make him proud to make me proud that jests!

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: So pair-taunt-like would I o’ersway his state,

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: That he should be my fool, and I his fate.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: None are so surely caught, when they are catched,

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: As wit turned fool. Folly, in wisdom hatched,

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Hath wisdom’s warrant and the help of school

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: And wit’s own grace to grace a learned fool.

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: The blood of youth burns not with such excess

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: As gravity’s revolt to wantonness.

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: Folly in fools bears not so strong a note

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: As fool’ry in the wise when wit doth dote,

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: Since all the power thereof it doth apply

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: To prove, by wit, worth in simplicity.
Enter Boyet.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Here comes Boyet, and mirth is in his face.

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: O, I am stabbed with laughter! Where’s her Grace?

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Thy news, Boyet?

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: Prepare, madam, prepare!

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: Arm, wenches, arm! Encounters mounted are

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: Against your peace. Love doth approach disguised,

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: Armed in arguments. You’ll be surprised.

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: Muster your wits, stand in your own defence,

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: Or hide your heads like cowards, and fly hence.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Saint Denis to Saint Cupid! What are they

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: That charge their breath against us? Say, scout, say.

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: Under the cool shade of a sycamore

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: I thought to close mine eyes some half an hour,

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: When, lo, to interrupt my purposed rest,

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: Toward that shade I might behold addressed

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: The King and his companions. Warily

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: I stole into a neighbour thicket by,

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: And overheard what you shall overhear:

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: That, by and by, disguised they will be here.

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: Their herald is a pretty knavish page

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: That well by heart hath conned his embassage.

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: Action and accent did they teach him there:

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: “Thus must thou speak,” and “thus thy body bear.”

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: And ever and anon they made a doubt

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: Presence majestical would put him out;

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: “For,” quoth the King, “an angel shalt thou see;

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: Yet fear not thou, but speak audaciously.”

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: The boy replied “An angel is not evil;

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: I should have feared her had she been a devil.”

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: With that all laughed and clapped him on the shoulder,

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: Making the bold wag by their praises bolder.

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: One rubbed his elbow thus, and fleered, and swore

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: A better speech was never spoke before.

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: Another with his finger and his thumb

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: Cried “_Via_, we will do ’t, come what will come.”

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: The third he capered, and cried “All goes well!”

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: The fourth turned on the toe, and down he fell.

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: With that they all did tumble on the ground,

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: With such a zealous laughter, so profound,

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: That in this spleen ridiculous appears,

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: To check their folly, passion’s solemn tears.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: But what, but what, come they to visit us?

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: They do, they do, and are apparelled thus,

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: Like Muscovites, or Russians, as I guess.

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: Their purpose is to parley, court, and dance,

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: And every one his love-feat will advance

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: Unto his several mistress, which they’ll know

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: By favours several which they did bestow.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: And will they so? The gallants shall be tasked;

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: For, ladies, we will every one be masked,

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: And not a man of them shall have the grace,

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Despite of suit, to see a lady’s face.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Hold, Rosaline, this favour thou shalt wear,

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: And then the King will court thee for his dear.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Hold, take thou this, my sweet, and give me thine,

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: So shall Berowne take me for Rosaline.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: And change you favours too; so shall your loves

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Woo contrary, deceived by these removes.

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: Come on, then, wear the favours most in sight.

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: But in this changing, what is your intent?

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: The effect of my intent is to cross theirs.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: They do it but in mocking merriment,

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: And mock for mock is only my intent.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Their several counsels they unbosom shall

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: To loves mistook, and so be mocked withal

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Upon the next occasion that we meet,

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: With visages displayed to talk and greet.

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: But shall we dance, if they desire us to’t?

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: No, to the death we will not move a foot,

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Nor to their penned speech render we no grace,

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: But while ’tis spoke each turn away her face.

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: Why, that contempt will kill the speaker’s heart,

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: And quite divorce his memory from his part.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Therefore I do it, and I make no doubt

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: The rest will ne’er come in, if he be out.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: There’s no such sport as sport by sport o’erthrown,

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: To make theirs ours and ours none but our own.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: So shall we stay, mocking intended game,

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: And they, well mocked, depart away with shame.
[_Sound trumpet, within._]

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: The trumpet sounds. Be masked; the maskers come.
[_The Ladies mask._]
Enter Blackamoors with music, Moth, with a speech, the King, Berowne, Longaville and Dumaine disguised.

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: _All hail, the richest beauties on the earth!_

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: Beauties no richer than rich taffeta.

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: _A holy parcel of the fairest dames_
[_The Ladies turn their backs to him._]

lines.text: _That ever turned their_—backs—_to mortal views!_

lines.text: _Their eyes_, villain, _their eyes._

lines.text: _That ever turned their eyes to mortal views.

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: Out_—

lines.text: True; out indeed.

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: _Out of your favours, heavenly spirits, vouchsafe

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: Not to behold_—

lines.text: _Once to behold_, rogue!

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: _Once to behold with your sun-beamed eyes—

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: With your sun-beamed eyes_—

lines.text: They will not answer to that epithet.

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: You were best call it “daughter-beamed eyes”.

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: They do not mark me, and that brings me out.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Is this your perfectness? Be gone, you rogue!
[_Exit Moth._]

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: What would these strangers? Know their minds, Boyet.

lines.text: If they do speak our language, ’tis our will

lines.text: That some plain man recount their purposes.

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: Know what they would.

lines.text: What would you with the Princess?

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Nothing but peace and gentle visitation.

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: What would they, say they?

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: Nothing but peace and gentle visitation.

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: Why, that they have, and bid them so be gone.

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: She says you have it, and you may be gone.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Say to her we have measured many miles

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: To tread a measure with her on this grass.

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: They say that they have measured many a mile

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: To tread a measure with you on this grass.

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: It is not so. Ask them how many inches

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: Is in one mile? If they have measured many,

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: The measure then of one is easily told.

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: If to come hither you have measured miles,

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: And many miles, the Princess bids you tell

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: How many inches doth fill up one mile.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Tell her we measure them by weary steps.

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: She hears herself.

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: How many weary steps

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: Of many weary miles you have o’ergone

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: Are numbered in the travel of one mile?

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: We number nothing that we spend for you.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Our duty is so rich, so infinite,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: That we may do it still without account.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Vouchsafe to show the sunshine of your face,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: That we, like savages, may worship it.

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: My face is but a moon, and clouded too.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Blessed are clouds, to do as such clouds do!

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Vouchsafe, bright moon, and these thy stars, to shine,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Those clouds removed, upon our watery eyne.

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: O vain petitioner! Beg a greater matter!

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: Thou now requests but moonshine in the water.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Then in our measure do but vouchsafe one change.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Thou bidd’st me beg; this begging is not strange.

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: Play, music, then! Nay, you must do it soon.
[_Music plays._]

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: Not yet? No dance! Thus change I like the moon.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Will you not dance? How come you thus estranged?

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: You took the moon at full, but now she’s changed.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Yet still she is the moon, and I the man.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: The music plays, vouchsafe some motion to it.

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: Our ears vouchsafe it.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: But your legs should do it.

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: Since you are strangers and come here by chance,

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: We’ll not be nice. Take hands. We will not dance.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Why take we hands then?

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: Only to part friends.

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: Curtsy, sweet hearts, and so the measure ends.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: More measure of this measure! Be not nice.

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: We can afford no more at such a price.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Price you yourselves? What buys your company?

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: Your absence only.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: That can never be.

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: Then cannot we be bought. And so adieu—

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: Twice to your visor, and half once to you!

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: If you deny to dance, let’s hold more chat.

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: In private then.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: I am best pleased with that.
[_They converse apart._]

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: White-handed mistress, one sweet word with thee.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Honey, and milk, and sugar: there is three.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Nay, then, two treys, an if you grow so nice,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Metheglin, wort, and malmsey. Well run, dice!

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: There’s half a dozen sweets.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Seventh sweet, adieu.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Since you can cog, I’ll play no more with you.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: One word in secret.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Let it not be sweet.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Thou griev’st my gall.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Gall! Bitter.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Therefore meet.
[_They converse apart._]

lines.speaker: DUMAINE
lines.text: Will you vouchsafe with me to change a word?

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: Name it.

lines.speaker: DUMAINE
lines.text: Fair lady—

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: Say you so? Fair lord!

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: Take that for your “fair lady”.

lines.speaker: DUMAINE
lines.text: Please it you,

lines.speaker: DUMAINE
lines.text: As much in private, and I’ll bid adieu.
[_They converse apart._]

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: What, was your visor made without a tongue?

lines.speaker: LONGAVILLE
lines.text: I know the reason, lady, why you ask.

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: O, for your reason! Quickly, sir, I long.

lines.speaker: LONGAVILLE
lines.text: You have a double tongue within your mask,

lines.speaker: LONGAVILLE
lines.text: And would afford my speechless visor half.

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: “Veal”, quoth the Dutchman. Is not veal a calf?

lines.speaker: LONGAVILLE
lines.text: A calf, fair lady?

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: No, a fair lord calf.

lines.speaker: LONGAVILLE
lines.text: Let’s part the word.

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: No, I’ll not be your half.

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: Take all and wean it; it may prove an ox.

lines.speaker: LONGAVILLE
lines.text: Look how you butt yourself in these sharp mocks.

lines.speaker: LONGAVILLE
lines.text: Will you give horns, chaste lady? Do not so.

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: Then die a calf before your horns do grow.

lines.speaker: LONGAVILLE
lines.text: One word in private with you ere I die.

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: Bleat softly, then; the butcher hears you cry.
[_They converse apart._]

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: The tongues of mocking wenches are as keen

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: As is the razor’s edge invisible,

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: Cutting a smaller hair than may be seen;

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: Above the sense of sense, so sensible

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: Seemeth their conference. Their conceits have wings

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: Fleeter than arrows, bullets, wind, thought, swifter things.

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: Not one word more, my maids; break off, break off.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: By heaven, all dry-beaten with pure scoff!

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Farewell, mad wenches. You have simple wits.
[_Exeunt King, Lords and Blackamoors._]

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Twenty adieus, my frozen Muscovites.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Are these the breed of wits so wondered at?

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: Tapers they are, with your sweet breaths puffed out.

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: Well-liking wits they have; gross, gross; fat, fat.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: O poverty in wit, kingly-poor flout!

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Will they not, think you, hang themselves tonight?

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Or ever but in vizors show their faces?

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: This pert Berowne was out of countenance quite.

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: They were all in lamentable cases.

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: The King was weeping-ripe for a good word.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Berowne did swear himself out of all suit.

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: Dumaine was at my service, and his sword.

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: “_Non point_,” quoth I; my servant straight was mute.

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: Lord Longaville said I came o’er his heart;

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: And trow you what he called me?

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Qualm, perhaps.

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: Yes, in good faith.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Go, sickness as thou art!

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: Well, better wits have worn plain statute-caps.

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: But will you hear? The King is my love sworn.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: And quick Berowne hath plighted faith to me.

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: And Longaville was for my service born.

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: Dumaine is mine as sure as bark on tree.

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: Madam, and pretty mistresses, give ear.

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: Immediately they will again be here

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: In their own shapes, for it can never be

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: They will digest this harsh indignity.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Will they return?

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: They will, they will, God knows,

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: And leap for joy, though they are lame with blows.

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: Therefore, change favours and, when they repair,

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: Blow like sweet roses in this summer air.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: How “blow”? How “blow”? Speak to be understood.

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: Fair ladies masked are roses in their bud.

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: Dismasked, their damask sweet commixture shown,

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: Are angels vailing clouds, or roses blown.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Avaunt, perplexity! What shall we do

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: If they return in their own shapes to woo?

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: Good madam, if by me you’ll be advised,

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: Let’s mock them still, as well known as disguised.

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: Let us complain to them what fools were here,

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: Disguised like Muscovites in shapeless gear;

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: And wonder what they were, and to what end

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: Their shallow shows and prologue vilely penned,

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: And their rough carriage so ridiculous,

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: Should be presented at our tent to us.

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: Ladies, withdraw. The gallants are at hand.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Whip to our tents, as roes run o’er the land.

lines.text: Fair sir, God save you. Where’s the Princess?

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: Gone to her tent. Please it your Majesty

lines.text: This fellow pecks up wit as pigeons peas

lines.speaker: BEROWNE

lines.text: At wakes and wassails, meetings, markets, fairs;

lines.text: This gallant pins the wenches on his sleeve.

lines.text: Had he been Adam, he had tempted Eve.

lines.text: He can carve too, and lisp. Why, this is he

lines.text: This is the ape of form, Monsieur the Nice,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: That, when he plays at tables, chides the dice

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: In honourable terms. Nay, he can sing

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: A mean most meanly; and in ushering

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Mend him who can. The ladies call him sweet.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: This is the flower that smiles on everyone,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: To show his teeth as white as whale’s bone;

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
