lines.text: A blister on his sweet tongue, with my heart,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: That put Armado’s page out of his part!
Enter the Princess, Rosaline, Maria, Katharine with Boyet.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: See where it comes! Behaviour, what wert thou

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Till this man showed thee, and what art thou now?

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: All hail, sweet madam, and fair time of day.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: “Fair” in “all hail” is foul, as I conceive.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Construe my speeches better, if you may.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Then wish me better. I will give you leave.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: We came to visit you, and purpose now

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: To lead you to our court. Vouchsafe it then.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: This field shall hold me, and so hold your vow.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Nor God nor I delights in perjured men.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Rebuke me not for that which you provoke.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: The virtue of your eye must break my oath.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: You nickname virtue: “vice” you should have spoke;

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: For virtue’s office never breaks men’s troth.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Now by my maiden honour, yet as pure

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: As the unsullied lily, I protest,

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: A world of torments though I should endure,

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: I would not yield to be your house’s guest,

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: So much I hate a breaking cause to be

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Of heavenly oaths, vowed with integrity.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: O, you have lived in desolation here,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Unseen, unvisited, much to our shame.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Not so, my lord. It is not so, I swear.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: We have had pastimes here and pleasant game.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: A mess of Russians left us but of late.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: How, madam? Russians?

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Ay, in truth, my lord.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Trim gallants, full of courtship and of state.

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: Madam, speak true. It is not so, my lord.

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: My lady, to the manner of the days,

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: In courtesy gives undeserving praise.

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: We four indeed confronted were with four

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: In Russian habit. Here they stayed an hour

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: And talked apace; and in that hour, my lord,

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: They did not bless us with one happy word.

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: I dare not call them fools; but this I think,

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: When they are thirsty, fools would fain have drink.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: This jest is dry to me. My gentle sweet,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Your wit makes wise things foolish. When we greet,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: With eyes’ best seeing, heaven’s fiery eye,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: By light we lose light. Your capacity

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Is of that nature that to your huge store

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Wise things seem foolish and rich things but poor.

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: This proves you wise and rich, for in my eye—

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: I am a fool, and full of poverty.

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: But that you take what doth to you belong,

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: It were a fault to snatch words from my tongue.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: O, I am yours, and all that I possess.

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: All the fool mine?

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: I cannot give you less.

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: Which of the visors was it that you wore?

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Where, when, what visor? Why demand you this?

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: There, then, that visor; that superfluous case

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: That hid the worse and showed the better face.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: We are descried. They’ll mock us now downright.

lines.speaker: DUMAINE
lines.text: Let us confess and turn it to a jest.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Amazed, my lord? Why looks your Highness sad?

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: Help! Hold his brows! He’ll swoon. Why look you pale?

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: Seasick, I think, coming from Muscovy.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Thus pour the stars down plagues for perjury.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Can any face of brass hold longer out?

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Here stand I, lady; dart thy skill at me.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Bruise me with scorn, confound me with a flout,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Thrust thy sharp wit quite through my ignorance,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Cut me to pieces with thy keen conceit,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: And I will wish thee never more to dance,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Nor never more in Russian habit wait.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: O, never will I trust to speeches penned,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Nor to the motion of a school-boy’s tongue,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Nor never come in visor to my friend,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Nor woo in rhyme like a blind harper’s song.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Taffeta phrases, silken terms precise,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Three-piled hyperboles, spruce affectation,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Figures pedantical: these summer flies

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Have blown me full of maggot ostentation.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: I do forswear them, and I here protest,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: By this white glove—how white the hand, God knows!—

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Henceforth my wooing mind shall be expressed

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: In russet yeas and honest kersey noes.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: And, to begin: wench, so God help me, law,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: My love to thee is sound, _sans_ crack or flaw.

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: _Sans_ “_sans_,” I pray you.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Yet I have a trick

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Of the old rage. Bear with me, I am sick;

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: I’ll leave it by degrees. Soft, let us see:

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Write “Lord have mercy on us” on those three.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: They are infected; in their hearts it lies;

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: They have the plague, and caught it of your eyes.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: These lords are visited. You are not free,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: For the Lord’s tokens on you do I see.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: No, they are free that gave these tokens to us.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Our states are forfeit. Seek not to undo us.

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: It is not so. For how can this be true,

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: That you stand forfeit, being those that sue?

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Peace! for I will not have to do with you.

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: Nor shall not, if I do as I intend.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Speak for yourselves. My wit is at an end.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Teach us, sweet madam, for our rude transgression

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Some fair excuse.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: The fairest is confession.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Were not you here but even now, disguised?

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Madam, I was.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: And were you well advised?

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: I was, fair madam.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: When you then were here,

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: What did you whisper in your lady’s ear?

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: That more than all the world I did respect her.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: When she shall challenge this, you will reject her.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Upon mine honour, no.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Peace, peace, forbear!

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Your oath once broke, you force not to forswear.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Despise me when I break this oath of mine.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: I will; and therefore keep it. Rosaline,

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: What did the Russian whisper in your ear?

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: Madam, he swore that he did hold me dear

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: As precious eyesight, and did value me

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: Above this world; adding thereto, moreover,

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: That he would wed me, or else die my lover.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: God give thee joy of him! The noble lord

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Most honourably doth uphold his word.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: What mean you, madam? By my life, my troth,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: I never swore this lady such an oath.

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: By heaven, you did! And to confirm it plain,

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: You gave me this. But take it, sir, again.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: My faith and this the Princess I did give.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: I knew her by this jewel on her sleeve.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Pardon me, sir, this jewel did she wear,

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: And Lord Berowne, I thank him, is my dear.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: What, will you have me, or your pearl again?

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Neither of either; I remit both twain.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: I see the trick on’t. Here was a consent,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Knowing aforehand of our merriment,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: To dash it like a Christmas comedy.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Some carry-tale, some please-man, some slight zany,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Some mumble-news, some trencher-knight, some Dick,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: That smiles his cheek in years and knows the trick

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: To make my lady laugh when she’s disposed,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Told our intents before; which once disclosed,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: The ladies did change favours, and then we,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Following the signs, wooed but the sign of she.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Now, to our perjury to add more terror,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: We are again forsworn in will and error.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Much upon this ’tis. [_To Boyet_.] And might not you

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Forestall our sport, to make us thus untrue?

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Do not you know my lady’s foot by th’ squier,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: And laugh upon the apple of her eye?

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: And stand between her back, sir, and the fire,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Holding a trencher, jesting merrily?

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: You put our page out. Go, you are allowed;

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Die when you will, a smock shall be your shroud.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: You leer upon me, do you? There’s an eye

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Wounds like a leaden sword.

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: Full merrily

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: Hath this brave manage, this career, been run.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Lo, he is tilting straight! Peace! I have done.
Enter Costard.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Welcome, pure wit! Thou part’st a fair fray.

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: O Lord, sir, they would know

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: Whether the three Worthies shall come in or no.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: What, are there but three?

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: No, sir; but it is vara fine,

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: For every one pursents three.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: And three times thrice is nine.

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: Not so, sir, under correction, sir, I hope it is not so.

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: You cannot beg us, sir, I can assure you, sir; we know what we know.

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: I hope, sir, three times thrice, sir—

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Is not nine?

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: Under correction, sir, we know whereuntil it doth amount.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: By Jove, I always took three threes for nine.

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: O Lord, sir, it were pity you should get your living by reckoning, sir.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: How much is it?

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: O Lord, sir, the parties themselves, the actors, sir, will show

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: whereuntil it doth amount. For mine own part, I am, as they say, but to

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: parfect one man in one poor man—Pompion the Great, sir.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Art thou one of the Worthies?

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: It pleased them to think me worthy of Pompey the Great. For mine own

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: part, I know not the degree of the Worthy, but I am to stand for him.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Go bid them prepare.

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: We will turn it finely off, sir; we will take some care.
[_Exit Costard._]

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Berowne, they will shame us. Let them not approach.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: We are shame-proof, my lord, and ’tis some policy

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: To have one show worse than the King’s and his company.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: I say they shall not come.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Nay, my good lord, let me o’errule you now.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: That sport best pleases that doth least know how,

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Where zeal strives to content, and the contents

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Die in the zeal of that which it presents;

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Their form confounded makes most form in mirth,

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: When great things labouring perish in their birth.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: A right description of our sport, my lord.
Enter Armado, the Braggart.

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: Anointed, I implore so much expense of thy royal sweet breath as will

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: utter a brace of words.
[_Armado and King talk apart._]

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Doth this man serve God?

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Why ask you?

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: He speaks not like a man of God his making.

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: That is all one, my fair, sweet, honey monarch; for, I protest, the

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: schoolmaster is exceeding fantastical; too, too vain, too, too vain.

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: But we will put it, as they say, to _fortuna de la guerra_. I wish you

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: the peace of mind, most royal couplement!
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Here is like to be a good presence of Worthies. He presents Hector of

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Troy; the swain, Pompey the Great; the parish curate, Alexander;

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Armado’s page, Hercules; the pedant, Judas Maccabaeus.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: _And if these four Worthies in their first show thrive,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: These four will change habits and present the other five._

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: There is five in the first show.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: You are deceived. ’Tis not so.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: The pedant, the braggart, the hedge-priest, the fool, and the boy.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Abate throw at novum, and the whole world again

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Cannot pick out five such, take each one in his vein.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: The ship is under sail, and here she comes amain.
Enter Costard as Pompey.

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: _I Pompey am_—

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: You lie, you are not he.

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: _I Pompey am_—

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: With leopard’s head on knee.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Well said, old mocker. I must needs be friends with thee.

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: _I Pompey am, Pompey surnamed the Big._

lines.speaker: DUMAINE
lines.text: The “Great”.

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: It is “Great”, sir; _Pompey surnamed the Great,

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: That oft in field, with targe and shield, did make my foe to sweat.

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: And travelling along this coast, I here am come by chance,

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: And lay my arms before the legs of this sweet lass of France._

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: If your ladyship would say, “Thanks, Pompey”, I had done.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Great thanks, great Pompey.

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: ’Tis not so much worth; but I hope I was perfect. I made a little fault

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: in “Great”.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: My hat to a halfpenny, Pompey proves the best Worthy.
Enter Nathaniel, the Curate, for Alexander.

lines.speaker: NATHANIEL
lines.text: _When in the world I lived, I was the world’s commander;

lines.speaker: NATHANIEL
lines.text: By east, west, north, and south, I spread my conquering might.

lines.speaker: NATHANIEL
lines.text: My scutcheon plain declares that I am Alisander._

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: Your nose says, no, you are not; for it stands to right.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Your nose smells “no” in this, most tender-smelling knight.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: The conqueror is dismayed. Proceed, good Alexander.

lines.speaker: NATHANIEL
lines.text: _When in the world I lived, I was the world’s commander_—

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: Most true; ’tis right. You were so, Alisander.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Pompey the Great—

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: Your servant, and Costard.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Take away the conqueror, take away Alisander.
[_To Sir Nathaniel_.]

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: O sir, you have overthrown Alisander the

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: Conqueror. You will be scraped out of the painted cloth for this. Your

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: lion, that holds his pole-axe sitting on a close-stool, will be given

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: to Ajax. He will be the ninth Worthy. A conqueror, and afeard to speak?

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: Run away for shame, Alisander. [_Nathaniel retires_.] There, an’t shall

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: please you, a foolish mild man; an honest man, look you, and soon

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: dashed. He is a marvellous good neighbour, faith, and a very good

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: bowler; but for Alisander, alas you see how ’tis—a little o’erparted.

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: But there are Worthies a-coming will speak their mind in some other

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: sort.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Stand aside, good Pompey.
Enter Holofernes, the Pedant, as Judas, and Moth, the Boy, as Hercules.

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: _Great Hercules is presented by this imp,

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: Whose club killed Cerberus, that three-headed_ canus,

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: _And when he was a babe, a child, a shrimp,

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: Thus did he strangle serpents in his_ manus.

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: Quoniam _he seemeth in minority_,

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: Ergo _I come with this apology._

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: Keep some state in thy exit, and vanish.
[_Moth retires._]

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: _Judas I am._—

lines.speaker: DUMAINE
lines.text: A Judas!

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: Not Iscariot, sir.

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: _Judas I am, ycleped Maccabaeus._

lines.speaker: DUMAINE
lines.text: Judas Maccabaeus clipped is plain Judas.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: A kissing traitor. How art thou proved Judas?

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: _Judas I am_—

lines.speaker: DUMAINE
lines.text: The more shame for you, Judas.

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: What mean you, sir?

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: To make Judas hang himself.

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: Begin, sir; you are my elder.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Well followed. Judas was hanged on an elder.

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: I will not be put out of countenance.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Because thou hast no face.

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: What is this?

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: A cittern-head.

lines.speaker: DUMAINE
lines.text: The head of a bodkin.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: A death’s face in a ring.

lines.speaker: LONGAVILLE
lines.text: The face of an old Roman coin, scarce seen.

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: The pommel of Caesar’s falchion.

lines.speaker: DUMAINE
lines.text: The carved-bone face on a flask.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Saint George’s half-cheek in a brooch.

lines.speaker: DUMAINE
lines.text: Ay, and in a brooch of lead.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Ay, and worn in the cap of a tooth-drawer.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: And now forward, for we have put thee in countenance.

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: You have put me out of countenance.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: False. We have given thee faces.

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: But you have outfaced them all.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: An thou wert a lion, we would do so.

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: Therefore, as he is an ass, let him go.

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: And so adieu, sweet Jude. Nay, why dost thou stay?

lines.speaker: DUMAINE
lines.text: For the latter end of his name.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: For the ass to the Jude? Give it him. Jud-as, away!

lines.speaker: HOLOFERNES
lines.text: This is not generous, not gentle, not humble.

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: A light for Monsieur Judas! It grows dark; he may stumble.
[_Exit Holofernes._]

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Alas, poor Maccabaeus, how hath he been baited!
Enter Armado, the Braggart, as Hector.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Hide thy head, Achilles. Here comes Hector in arms.

lines.speaker: DUMAINE
lines.text: Though my mocks come home by me, I will now be merry.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Hector was but a Trojan in respect of this.

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: But is this Hector?

lines.speaker: DUMAINE
lines.text: I think Hector was not so clean-timbered.

lines.speaker: LONGAVILLE
lines.text: His leg is too big for Hector’s.

lines.speaker: DUMAINE
lines.text: More calf, certain.

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: No, he is best endued in the small.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: This cannot be Hector.

lines.speaker: DUMAINE
lines.text: He’s a god or a painter, for he makes faces.

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: _The armipotent Mars, of lances the almighty,

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: Gave Hector a gift_—

lines.speaker: DUMAINE
lines.text: A gilt nutmeg.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: A lemon.

lines.speaker: LONGAVILLE
lines.text: Stuck with cloves.

lines.speaker: DUMAINE
lines.text: No, cloven.

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: Peace!

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: _The armipotent Mars, of lances the almighty,

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: Gave Hector a gift, the heir of Ilion;

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: A man so breathed that certain he would fight, yea,

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: From morn till night, out of his pavilion.

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: I am that flower_—

lines.speaker: DUMAINE
lines.text: That mint.

lines.speaker: LONGAVILLE
lines.text: That columbine.

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: Sweet Lord Longaville, rein thy tongue.

lines.speaker: LONGAVILLE
lines.text: I must rather give it the rein, for it runs against Hector.

lines.speaker: DUMAINE
lines.text: Ay, and Hector’s a greyhound.

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: The sweet war-man is dead and rotten. Sweet chucks, beat not the bones

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: of the buried. When he breathed, he was a man. But I will forward with

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: my device. [_To the Princess_.] Sweet royalty, bestow on me the sense

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: of hearing.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Speak, brave Hector; we are much delighted.

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: I do adore thy sweet Grace’s slipper.

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: Loves her by the foot.

lines.speaker: DUMAINE
lines.text: He may not by the yard.

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: _This Hector far surmounted Hannibal.

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: The party is gone_—

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: Fellow Hector, she is gone; she is two months on her way.

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: What meanest thou?

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: Faith, unless you play the honest Trojan, the poor wench is cast away.

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: She’s quick; the child brags in her belly already. ’Tis yours.

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: Dost thou infamonize me among potentates? Thou shalt die.

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: Then shall Hector be whipped for Jaquenetta that is quick by him, and

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: hanged for Pompey that is dead by him.

lines.speaker: DUMAINE
lines.text: Most rare Pompey!

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: Renowned Pompey!

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Greater than  “Great”! Great, great, great Pompey! Pompey the Huge!

lines.speaker: DUMAINE
lines.text: Hector trembles.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Pompey is moved. More Ates, more Ates! Stir them on, stir them on!

lines.speaker: DUMAINE
lines.text: Hector will challenge him.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Ay, if he have no more man’s blood in his belly than will sup a flea.

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: By the north pole, I do challenge thee.

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: I will not fight with a pole, like a northern man. I’ll slash, I’ll do

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: it by the sword. I bepray you, let me borrow my arms again.

lines.speaker: DUMAINE
lines.text: Room for the incensed Worthies!

lines.speaker: COSTARD
lines.text: I’ll do it in my shirt.

lines.speaker: DUMAINE
lines.text: Most resolute Pompey!

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: Master, let me take you a buttonhole lower. Do you not see Pompey is

lines.speaker: MOTH
lines.text: uncasing for the combat? What mean you? You will lose your reputation.

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: Gentlemen and soldiers, pardon me. I will not combat in my shirt.

lines.speaker: DUMAINE
lines.text: You may not deny it. Pompey hath made the challenge.

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: Sweet bloods, I both may and will.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: What reason have you for ’t?

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: The naked truth of it is, I have no shirt. I go woolward for penance.

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: True, and it was enjoined him in Rome for want of linen; since when,

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: I’ll be sworn, he wore none but a dishclout of Jaquenetta’s, and that

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: he wears next his heart for a favour.
Enter a Messenger, Monsieur Marcadé.

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: MARCADÉ.

lines.speaker: BOYET
lines.text: God save you, madam.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Welcome, Marcadé,

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: But that thou interruptest our merriment.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: MARCADÉ.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: I am sorry, madam, for the news I bring

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Is heavy in my tongue. The King your father—

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Dead, for my life!

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: MARCADÉ.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Even so. My tale is told.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Worthies away! The scene begins to cloud.

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: For mine own part, I breathe free breath. I have seen the day of wrong

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: through the little hole of discretion, and I will right myself like a

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: soldier.
[_Exeunt Worthies._]

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: How fares your Majesty?

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Boyet, prepare. I will away tonight.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Madam, not so. I do beseech you stay.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Prepare, I say. I thank you, gracious lords,

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: For all your fair endeavours, and entreat,

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Out of a new-sad soul, that you vouchsafe

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: In your rich wisdom to excuse or hide

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: The liberal opposition of our spirits,

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: If over-boldly we have borne ourselves

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: In the converse of breath; your gentleness

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Was guilty of it. Farewell, worthy lord!

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: A heavy heart bears not a nimble tongue.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Excuse me so, coming too short of thanks

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: For my great suit so easily obtained.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: The extreme parts of time extremely forms

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: All causes to the purpose of his speed,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: And often at his very loose decides

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: That which long process could not arbitrate.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: And though the mourning brow of progeny

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Forbid the smiling courtesy of love

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: The holy suit which fain it would convince,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Yet, since love’s argument was first on foot,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Let not the cloud of sorrow jostle it

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: From what it purposed; since to wail friends lost

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Is not by much so wholesome-profitable

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: As to rejoice at friends but newly found.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: I understand you not. My griefs are double.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Honest plain words best pierce the ear of grief;

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: And by these badges understand the King.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: For your fair sakes have we neglected time,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Played foul play with our oaths. Your beauty, ladies,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Hath much deformed us, fashioning our humours

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Even to the opposed end of our intents;

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: And what in us hath seemed ridiculous—

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: As love is full of unbefitting strains,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: All wanton as a child, skipping and vain,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Formed by the eye and therefore, like the eye,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Full of strange shapes, of habits and of forms,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Varying in subjects as the eye doth roll

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: To every varied object in his glance;

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Which parti-coated presence of loose love

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Put on by us, if, in your heavenly eyes,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Have misbecomed our oaths and gravities,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Those heavenly eyes that look into these faults

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Suggested us to make. Therefore, ladies,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Our love being yours, the error that love makes

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Is likewise yours. We to ourselves prove false

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: By being once false for ever to be true

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: To those that make us both—fair ladies, you.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: And even that falsehood, in itself a sin,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Thus purifies itself and turns to grace.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: We have received your letters, full of love;

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Your favours, the ambassadors of love;

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: And in our maiden council rated them

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: At courtship, pleasant jest, and courtesy,

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: As bombast and as lining to the time.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: But more devout than this in our respects

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Have we not been; and therefore met your loves

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: In their own fashion, like a merriment.

lines.speaker: DUMAINE
lines.text: Our letters, madam, showed much more than jest.

lines.speaker: LONGAVILLE
lines.text: So did our looks.

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: We did not quote them so.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Now, at the latest minute of the hour,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Grant us your loves.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: A time, methinks, too short

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: To make a world-without-end bargain in.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: No, no, my lord, your Grace is perjured much,

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Full of dear guiltiness; and therefore this:

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: If for my love—as there is no such cause—

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: You will do aught, this shall you do for me:

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Your oath I will not trust, but go with speed

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: To some forlorn and naked hermitage,

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Remote from all the pleasures of the world,

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: There stay until the twelve celestial signs

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Have brought about the annual reckoning.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: If this austere insociable life

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Change not your offer made in heat of blood;

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: If frosts and fasts, hard lodging and thin weeds,

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Nip not the gaudy blossoms of your love,

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: But that it bear this trial, and last love;

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Then, at the expiration of the year,

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Come challenge me, challenge me by these deserts,

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: And, by this virgin palm now kissing thine,

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: I will be thine. And, till that instance, shut

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: My woeful self up in a mournful house,

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Raining the tears of lamentation

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: For the remembrance of my father’s death.

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: If this thou do deny, let our hands part,

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Neither entitled in the other’s heart.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: If this, or more than this, I would deny,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: To flatter up these powers of mine with rest,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: The sudden hand of death close up mine eye!

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Hence hermit, then. My heart is in thy breast.
[_They converse apart_]

lines.speaker: DUMAINE
lines.text: And what to me, my love? But what to me?

lines.speaker: DUMAINE
lines.text: A wife?

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: A beard, fair health, and honesty;

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: With threefold love I wish you all these three.

lines.speaker: DUMAINE
lines.text: O, shall I say, “I thank you, gentle wife”?

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: No so, my lord. A twelvemonth and a day

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: I’ll mark no words that smooth-faced wooers say.

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: Come when the King doth to my lady come;

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: Then, if I have much love, I’ll give you some.

lines.speaker: DUMAINE
lines.text: I’ll serve thee true and faithfully till then.

lines.speaker: KATHARINE
lines.text: Yet swear not, lest ye be forsworn again.
[_They converse apart_]

lines.speaker: LONGAVILLE
lines.text: What says Maria?

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: At the twelvemonth’s end

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: I’ll change my black gown for a faithful friend.

lines.speaker: LONGAVILLE
lines.text: I’ll stay with patience, but the time is long.

lines.speaker: MARIA
lines.text: The liker you; few taller are so young.
[_They converse apart_]

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Studies my lady? Mistress, look on me.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Behold the window of my heart, mine eye,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: What humble suit attends thy answer there.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Impose some service on me for thy love.

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: Oft have I heard of you, my Lord Berowne,

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: Before I saw you; and the world’s large tongue

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: Proclaims you for a man replete with mocks,

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: Full of comparisons and wounding flouts,

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: Which you on all estates will execute

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: That lie within the mercy of your wit.

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: To weed this wormwood from your fruitful brain,

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: And therewithal to win me, if you please,

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: Without the which I am not to be won,

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: You shall this twelvemonth term from day to day

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: Visit the speechless sick, and still converse

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: With groaning wretches; and your task shall be,

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: With all the fierce endeavour of your wit

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: To enforce the pained impotent to smile.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: To move wild laughter in the throat of death?

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: It cannot be, it is impossible.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Mirth cannot move a soul in agony.

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: Why, that’s the way to choke a gibing spirit,

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: Whose influence is begot of that loose grace

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: Which shallow laughing hearers give to fools.

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: A jest’s prosperity lies in the ear

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: Of him that hears it, never in the tongue

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: Of him that makes it. Then, if sickly ears,

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: Deafed with the clamours of their own dear groans,

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: Will hear your idle scorns, continue then,

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: And I will have you and that fault withal;

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: But if they will not, throw away that spirit,

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: And I shall find you empty of that fault,

lines.speaker: ROSALINE
lines.text: Right joyful of your reformation.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: A twelvemonth? Well, befall what will befall,

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: I’ll jest a twelvemonth in an hospital.
[_To the King_.]

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Ay, sweet my lord, and so I take my leave.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: No, madam, we will bring you on your way.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Our wooing doth not end like an old play.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Jack hath not Jill. These ladies’ courtesy

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: Might well have made our sport a comedy.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Come, sir, it wants a twelvemonth and a day,

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: And then ’twill end.

lines.speaker: BEROWNE
lines.text: That’s too long for a play.
Enter Armado, the Braggart.

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: Sweet Majesty, vouchsafe me—

lines.speaker: PRINCESS
lines.text: Was not that Hector?

lines.speaker: DUMAINE
lines.text: The worthy knight of Troy.

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: I will kiss thy royal finger, and take leave. I am a votary; I have

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: vowed to Jaquenetta to hold the plough for her sweet love three year.

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: But, most esteemed Greatness, will you hear the dialogue that the two

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: learned men have compiled in praise of the owl and the cuckoo? It

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: should have followed in the end of our show.

lines.speaker: KING
lines.text: Call them forth quickly; we will do so.

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: Holla! Approach.
Enter all.

lines.text: This side is _Hiems_, Winter; this _Ver_, the Spring; the one

lines.speaker: ARMADO
lines.text: maintained by the owl, th’ other by the cuckoo. _Ver_, begin.

lines.text: Mocks married men; for thus sings he:

lines.text: “Cuckoo!

lines.text: The cuckoo then, on every tree,

lines.text: Then nightly sings the staring owl:
